title: Church and the Poor
definition: Church and the Poor teaches the Church's responsibility to show mercy, generosity, justice, and practical concern for those in need.
summary: The Church must not separate Gospel truth from mercy toward the poor.
christFocus: Jesus Christ identified with the lowly and calls His people to serve the least with love.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Church and the Poor teaches that Christ does not redeem people into isolation but into a gathered, accountable, worshiping, serving, and mission-shaped people. The Church belongs to Jesus, is formed by the Gospel, and is strengthened by the Word, prayer, ordinances, fellowship, and Spirit-empowered service.

This doctrine helps believers see the Church as more than a place to attend. It is the household of God, the body of Christ, and a visible witness to the grace, holiness, unity, and truth of the Lord.

The specific emphasis here is the church must not separate gospel truth from mercy toward the poor.. A healthy church life displays Christ's care for His people and His mission to the world.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because many people treat church as optional, consumer-driven, or disconnected from discipleship. Church and the Poor calls believers back to Christ's design for His people, where worship, truth, love, accountability, service, and mission are held together.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Participate in church life with humility and faithfulness. Let church and the poor move you to serve, forgive, gather, pray, give, submit to Scripture, care for others, and help the body of Christ grow in love and maturity.
